Jason

messages.subject: featureCounts 1.5.0 no longer automatically resort paired-end BAM files
messages.subject_clean: featureCounts 1.5.0 no longer automatically resort paired-end BAM files
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

congratulations on a great piece of software!

I have just downloaded the latest featureCounts 1.5.0 and tried it on paired-end data. Previous versions of featureCounts detected that the BAM file was sorted by coordinates and automatically re-sorted it before counting. The new featureCounts does not resort the BAM files, and as a result it can assign 0.1% of the reads only. However, if I first use the new "repair" utility, and then run featureCounts on the output of such utility, everything works fine. The manual still mentions that featureCounts can automatically resort BAM files if needed, so I guess that manually calling "repair" is just a temporary workaround..?

Thank you for your feedback.

Best,

Roberto

messages.subject_clean: featureCounts 1.5.0 no longer automatically resort paired-end BAM files
messages.body_plain:
Dear Roberto,

featureCounts 1.5.0 still automatically re-sorts the reads if it detects any read pair that is not adjacent to each other in the input. Could you please provide more details about your data such as how your bam file was generated and also your command? This will help figure out what may cause the issue you encountered.

The 'repair' program is a new program included in 1.5.0 release. It is particularly useful for those users who want to perform an one-off conversion of location-sorted read pairs to name-sorted reads pairs and then run featureCounts on the converted data.

Best wishes,

Wei

messages.subject_clean: featureCounts 1.5.0 no longer automatically resort paired-end BAM files
messages.body_plain:
Hi Wei,

thank you for your response.

I use STAR to generate BAM files sorted by coordinates:

STAR --genomeDir /opt/ngs_indexes/star/mm10.primary_assembly.gencode.vM6_refchrom.50bp --runThreadN 4 --genomeLoad LoadAndKeep --readFilesIn R1.fastq R2.fastq --outSAMunmapped Within --outSAMtype BAM SortedByCoordinate --limitBAMsortRAM 17179869184 --outFilterType BySJout --outFilterMultimapNmax 20 --alignSJoverhangMin 8 --alignSJDBoverhangMin 1 --outFilterMismatchNmax 999 --outFilterMismatchNoverLmax 0.04 --alignIntronMin 20 --alignIntronMax 1000000 --alignMatesGapMax 1000000 --seedSearchStartLmax 30

which are then filtered:

samtools view -F 2828 -f 2 -q 30 -@ 4 -b mappings.bam >filtered_mappings.bam

Typically, filter_mappings.bam is then fed to featureCounts:

featureCounts -T 12 -s 2 -p -B -C -P -d 40 -D 4000 -t exon -g gene_id -a /opt/ngs_indexes/models/mm/mm10/gencode.vM6.refchrom.annotation.gtf -o counts.txt *.bam

This pipeline resulted in re-sorting from previous versions of featureCounts with 80-95% of features assigned, whereas now there is no automatic re-sorting and only 0.1% of features gets assigned.

Thank you,

Roberto

Hi Roberto,

Thanks for providing further information. We found that there is a bug in featureCounts introduced in 1.5.0 which resulted in incorrect read counting when '-P' option is turned on. We will release a patched version with this bug fixed in the next few days. For now, you should run repair program before running featureCounts. When the new version is available, you can directly run featureCounts on your data.

Sorry for the inconvenience caused.

Wei

messages.subject: Change in behavior of -R flag for featureCounts in version 1.5.0
messages.subject_clean: Change in behavior of -R flag for featureCounts in version 1.5.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I like to use the -R flag for featureCounts to report the assignment results per read. In version 1.4.4, it saved these results based on the input file name. For example, it saved the results in DIRNAME/FILENAME.featureCounts. I recently updated to version 1.5.0. Now instead of saving this output file in the same directory as the input file, it concatenates the directory and filename to save the file in the current working directory, e.g. DIRNAME.FILENAME.featureCounts. This is very inconvenient. The output of the program should not change based on the directory where I happen to run it.

Is it possible to return the -R flag to its previous behavior? Even better would be to allow the user to specify a filename to save these results. Personally I'd prefer to this file saved to the same place as the output file, not the input file. Allowing -R to accept a filename would allow each individual end user to save these results wherever they like.

Thanks,

John

messages.subject: Segmentation fault with subread-align 1.5.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am remapping my fastq files with the new 1.5.0 version of subread-align. Overall this has been successful. Out of a total of 2,664 fastq files, 2,356 ran without a problem. I am trying to figure out why the remaining files do not work with the latest version of Subread.

Here is how I ran subread-align v1.4.4 before. The input was a gzipped fastq, the output is bam. I only report uniquely mapping reads (-u) and use the Hamming distance to break ties (-H).

# Using version 1.4.4 with a genome indexed with buildindex from 1.4.4
subread-align -i $GENOME -r $FILE --gzFASTQinput --BAMoutput -uH > $OUTDIR/$BASE.bam

To obtain similar results with v1.5.0, I re-ran subread-buildindex and translated to the following for v1.5.0. The input is still a gzipped fastq and output bam. I still only report uniquely mapping reads, and the Hamming distance is used to break ties (at least according to the log sent to stderr. I assume this is now the only option since -H is no longer a flag).

# Using version 1.5.0 with a genome indexed with buildindex from 1.5.0
subread-align -i $GENOME -r $FILE -t 0 -u > $OUTDIR/$BASE.bam

So I guess first question is, did I translate this properly from v1.4.4 to v1.5.0?

I've created two test files to help isolate the problem. test-pass.fastq.gz works with both v1.4.4 and v1.5.0. test-fail.fastq.gz only works v1.4.4. Both test files contain 866,657 reads (3,466,628 lines). The reads in the two files are mutually-exclusive, but they are both subsets from the same sequencing run. The data is single end collected from humans. The reads have been quality trimmed, so they are varying lengths (20 bp <= length < 100 bp). I've placed them in my Dropbox Public folder for download:

https://www.dropbox.com/s/n20axbjlel8mhxz/test-pass.fastq.gz?dl=0
https://www.dropbox.com/s/b97f7otznmkzzfp/test-fail.fastq.gz?dl=0

I've attached the stderr from running test-fail.fastq.gz and test-pass.fastq.gz using either v1.4.4 or v1.5.0. These were run sequentially on the same compute node with 12g of RAM.

I checked to see if there was a difference in the number of very short reads (20 bp), but there is not a substantial difference between the two test files.

Can you identify what is causing the segmentation fault? Please let me know if there is any other information you would like me to provide.

Thanks,

John

messages.subject_clean: Differences in mapping algorithm in version 1.5.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Is there a plan to describe the latest changes to the mapping algorithm used in version 1.5.0? According to the SourceForge <http://subread.sourceforge.net/> page, there are two main new updates to subread-align:
New parameter '--type' for sequencing-type-specific mapping optimization.
Improved detection of multi-mapping reads by considering locations that receive second highest votes.
But I couldn't find anywhere in the Users Guide <http://bioinf.wehi.edu.au/subread-package/SubreadUsersGuide.pdf> that details the new features and how they will affect mapping results.

I noticed that there were a decent number of differences in my mapping results obtained from v1.4.4 and v1.5.0. I've cherry-picked a few examples from the mapping of the fastq file from my last post <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/subread/gueV7zD37GY>. Below are links to the bam files.

https://www.dropbox.com/s/fk61awkum3jecf4/test-pass-v1.5.0.bam?dl=0

messages.subject: Re: Segmentation fault with subread-align 1.5.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi John,

Many thanks for providing the data. We found that the seg fault was caused by a bug in implementing a new function for reading in gzipped fastq files in version 1.5.0 (1.5.0 processes gzipped fastq files more efficiently than previous versions). We have fixed this bug and are working on releasing a patched version this week.

Cheers,
Wei

messages.subject: Re: Differences in mapping algorithm in version 1.5.0
messages.subject_clean: Differences in mapping algorithm in version 1.5.0
messages.body_plain:
We will add more detailed descriptions to the '--type' parameter and also to our recent improvement on mapping multi-mapping reads in the users guide in the next release.

It has been nearly two years between the releases of versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.0, so there will be some differences between them. It is good to see v1.5.0 gave you better mapping result compared to v1.4.4 in your Example #1.

For your example #2, although the read was mapped to chr2 by v1.5.0, it was mapped to a location different from that reported by BLAT. You will need to check the CIGAR string reported by 1.5.0 to see how many bases were successfully aligned in the read. I bet it should a lot more than 20.

For example #3, it is hard to tell what caused the 1 base difference in mapping location without seeing the CIGAR strings. This could be caused by soft-clipping or presence of an indel. Again, it will be helpful if you can show the CIGAR for these mappings.

Cheers,
Wei
